request.prompt: View 3, the same town as the reference image, Kelderby as a straight-down plan from directly overhead, north at the top of the frame, in the same hand and the same late-afternoon light with shadows falling to the east. At the top, the green mountain with the castle on its summit: a square grey courtyard castle with a gatehouse tower, a hall range and a kitchen tower along its north side, a cobbled courtyard and a curtain wall. A cobbled road zig-zags down the mountain from the castle to a rectangular cobbled square at the mountain's foot, near the upper middle of the frame. On the square's east side the cross-shaped roof of a large cathedral with its long nave running east and a walled churchyard to its south; on the square's west side the L-shaped roof of a coaching inn around its yard. From the square's south side one broad straight main street runs due south down the middle of the frame to a long straight stone quay along the harbour basin at the bottom; tiled roofs of houses and yards line both sides of the street, and three narrow side lanes leave it east and west. The lowest lane on the east runs out to a cliff path that follows the spine of a rocky headland south, on the east side of the harbour basin, to a white round lighthouse with a cottage in a walled yard at its southern tip. Deep blue sea at the bottom and right; the coast curving away on the left.
request.style_note: Kelderby, a cheerful stone-and-timber harbour town on the slope below a castle mountain, on the afternoon of its yearly Founders' Play, drawn in the same hand throughout: warm painterly storybook concept painting, bright and friendly, clear sky, golden late-afternoon sun from the west, honey light on grey stone-brick walls and dark spruce and oak timber, dark slate-blue tile roofs, a deep blue sea, green turf and flower boxes of red poppies, blue cornflowers and white daisies, strings of bright festival bunting and painted banners strung across the streets for the play. Everything is massed from large squared blocks with flat faces and clean right angles so every form could be built block by block in Minecraft: the houses are rectangular stone boxes with timber upper storeys and steep gable roofs, the main street is a broad cobbled street stepping down the slope in short flights of shallow steps, the quay is a straight stone wall with square bollards. People, where any appear, are ordinary townsfolk in plain wool, linen and aprons, never armoured, never armed. Nothing glows but lanterns and windows. Each image is ONE single full-frame view of that place, filling the frame edge to edge: never a sheet, never a grid, never a panel, never an inset, never a caption, label, text or border.
